To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a thiorphane-sensitive mechanism regulates the intensity and the duration of the inhibiting activity of both endogenous and exogenous CGRP in guinea pig ureter.
a thiorphansensitive mechanism regulates the action, intensity and duration of both exogenous (h alpha CG RP) and endogenous CG RP in the guinea pig ureter.
a neutral endopeptidine-sensitive mechanism regulates the intensity and the duration of the inhibiting action of both endogenous and exogenous CGRP in guinea-pig urinary bladder.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of calcitonin-gene related peptide (CGRP)-containing nerve fibers in the regulation of ureteral motility.
the study of the mechanisms regulating the intensity of action of calcitoni gene-related peptide (alpha-CGRP) in the smooth muscle of the guinea pig ureter.
the existence of mechanisms for inactivation and/or degradation of calcitonin-like peptides in the guinea pig isolated ureter.

the CGRP inhibitory effect is potentiated by thiorphan, an inhibitor of neutral endopetidase, while captopil and bestain, inhibitors of angiotensin converting enzyme and aminopeptidase M respectively, were without effect.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the inhibitory activity exerted by exogenous CGRP on ureteral smooth muscle is potentiated by the inhibition of the activity of a peptidase, presumably neutral endopetidase, while the inhibitory activity produced by endogenous peptide is potentiated by inhibition of neutral endopep-tidase.
the action of CGRP in the ureter is modulated by the action of thiorphan-sensitive mechanisms.
